blocks.text: Imagine visiting a website. Behind the scenes, your browser and the web server are having a conversation using HTTP. Let's explore how this protocol works and why it's crucial for the web.

blocks.markdown: The Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) is the foundation of data communication on the World Wide Web. It defines how messages are formatted and transmitted, and how web servers and browsers should respond to various commands.

blocks.title: HTTP Request
blocks.text: An HTTP request is a message sent by a client to a server to request a resource. It consists of a request line, headers, and an optional body.

blocks.caption: Example of an HTTP GET request

blocks.title: Understanding an HTTP Request
blocks.prompt: Analyze the following HTTP request and identify its components: `GET /home HTTP/1.1\nHost: example.com\nAccept: text/html`

steps.text: Determine the method: `GET`, the path: `/home`, and the HTTP version: `HTTP/1.1`.
List the headers: `Host: example.com` and `Accept: text/html`.

blocks.answer: The request line is `GET /home HTTP/1.1`, the method is `GET`, the path is `/home`, and the HTTP version is `HTTP/1.1`. The headers are `Host: example.com` and `Accept: text/html`.

blocks.title: HTTP Response
blocks.text: An HTTP response is a message sent by a server to a client in response to an HTTP request. It consists of a status line, headers, and an optional body.

blocks.title: Interpreting an HTTP Response
blocks.prompt: Analyze the following HTTP response and identify its components: `HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found\nContent-Type: text/html\nContent-Length: 0`

steps.text: Identify the status line: `HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found`.
Determine the HTTP version: `HTTP/1.1`, the status code: `404`, and the reason phrase: `Not Found`.

blocks.answer: The status line is `HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found`, the HTTP version is `HTTP/1.1`, the status code is `404`, and the reason phrase is `Not Found`. The headers are `Content-Type: text/html` and `Content-Length: 0`.

blocks.title: HTTP Status Codes
blocks.text: HTTP status codes are divided into five classes: 1xx (Informational), 2xx (Success), 3xx (Redirection), 4xx (Client Error), and 5xx (Server Error).

blocks.markdown: Caching is a mechanism to store copies of resources to reduce load times and server load. HTTP headers like `Cache-Control` and `Expires` manage caching behavior.

blocks.title: Caching in HTTP
blocks.prompt: Explain how the `Cache-Control: max-age=3600` header affects caching.

steps.text: The `Cache-Control` header specifies directives for caching mechanisms in both requests and responses.
The `max-age=3600` directive indicates that the resource is considered fresh for 3600 seconds (1 hour).

blocks.answer: The `Cache-Control: max-age=3600` header instructs caches that the resource can be served from the cache for up to 3600 seconds without revalidation.

blocks.title: Caching Pitfalls
blocks.text: Improper caching configurations can lead to stale data being served to users. Ensure cache directives align with the data's freshness requirements.

points: HTTP requests and responses are the core of web communication, with specific structures and components.
HTTP status codes provide information about the result of a request, categorized into five classes.
Caching reduces load times and server load, controlled via HTTP headers like `Cache-Control`.
